mechanism: Retail sales track household goods spending, the largest part of consumption. Firm sales growth supports company revenues and earnings (risk-on); slowing sales are an early sign of softening consumer demand.
key_finding: As known at the time (real-time RSXFS vintages), the rule selected on in-sample data uses yoy_zscore_60m / T_z_0 at L8 (IS Sharpe 0.90); test-period Sharpe 0.55 versus buy-and-hold SPY 1.00.
caveats: The strategy is search-selected and needs a frozen-rule holdout confirmation.
Retail sales are nominal and the advance estimate is revised in later reports, so the as-known-at-the-time and revised tracks differ through revisions as well as release timing.
Retail sales are broadly coincident with the business cycle, so a long apparent lead needs scrutiny.
The 2020-21 collapse and rebound in retail sales is an extreme outlier inside the test window.
The test window was seen by the previously published runs, so it is not a frozen hold-out.
narrative_summary: Retail sales ex food services (RSXFS) growth is tested as a procyclical consumer-demand overlay for SPY, not as a clean leading indicator.

data_provenance.source: FRED / ALFRED (U.S. Census Bureau, Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey)
